claims.claim: The note gives an unconditional four-evaluation example; its performance/error statements remain attributed.
claims.disposition: Qualify the binding assumptions; do not report measured cost or error repetition.

claims.claim: Fact variables select source facts through nil policy, filters and complements.
claims.disposition: Presence in an input instance is not sufficient for binding.

claims.claim: Implicit filtering is an explicit variable-set choice and can constrain combinations by uncovered aspects.
claims.disposition: Use explicit false in the local example; no assumed default.

claims.claim: Satisfied preconditions and the three special cases govern whether a variable-set evaluation occurs.
claims.disposition: Failure to evaluate is not automatically duplicate elimination.

claims.claim: Variable-set identity compares fact-variable evaluations; sequence order alone does not distinguish them.
claims.disposition: Do not replace fact identity with numeric equality.

claims.claim: Without sequence binding, each selected nonempty fact sequence permits individual facts, subject to evaluation rules.
claims.disposition: This supports the conditional four-data-set example.

claims.claim: Sequence binding has same-uncovered-aspect-set/equivalence, occurrence, maximality and matches constraints.
claims.disposition: Sequence binding alone does not universally collapse duplicates.

claims.claim: With matches omitted or false, aspect-matched facts cannot occur together in a sequence-bound result.
claims.disposition: The all-duplicates sequence example must state matches=true.

claims.claim: Empty sources without fallback cannot evaluate; fallback expressions cannot reference fact/general variables.
claims.disposition: Fallback does not make the simple product unconditional.

claims.claim: Different variable-set evaluations form different value-assertion data sets; their tests are effective Boolean values.
claims.disposition: Different data sets need not produce different Boolean results.

claims.claim: Validation says an assertion MAY be evaluated once for each data set; this is not a mandatory call count.
claims.disposition: No conclusion about a particular processor or conformance suite.

claims.claim: Formula-expression evaluation and optional output-fact construction are separate from value-assertion tests.
claims.disposition: Do not conflate Formula output facts with assertion errors.

claims.claim: The retained XPath2 XDM gives each node unique identity and preserves it in sequences.
claims.disposition: Numeric equality and author-assigned XML IDs do not establish node identity.
